title: This Stock Is Undervalued
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
summary: Joseph Carlson previews the second week of earnings season — SpaceX, Netflix, Meta, Tesla and Moody's all report — against growing AI-bubble concern, then criticises Brad Gerstner for talking bullish on TV while cutting Altimeter's exposure to its lowest in three years, and names ESPN (Disney) fail of the week over its embrace of gambling sponsorships. On SpaceX he is positive on the company (Starlink connectivity best, +65%) but at a $2.56T cap vs $12B trailing revenue he prefers Amazon ($775B revenue, AWS alone $148B) — SPCX and AMZN UNCERTAIN. Netflix is his 8th-largest holding: at 19x forward earnings he holds his full position into earnings with cautious optimism, argues the engagement-problem narrative misreads the Warner Bros bid, watch-time reporting and the 6% layoffs (whose memo reaffirmed full-year guidance), and sees a rerating to ~25x — NFLX HOLD, a BUY→HOLD change from his 5 Oct add with the bullish thesis intact. Meta is a HOLD through the capex cycle on monetisation power (ad price +12%, impressions +14%, ad revenue +27%). Tesla is an AVOID at 154x forward earnings on flat fundamentals and a slow robotaxi rollout. The undervalued stock of the title is Moody's: one of the best companies in the market and 'a particularly strong investment' right now — MCO BUY (first tracked). ASML is a passing analogy (bought sub-$700 after its 2025 narrative selloff) — UNCERTAIN.

calls.stance_flip: BUY->HOLD (holding full position, no new buy in this video; bullish thesis reiterated after the 5 Oct add)
calls.price_at_call: 19x forward P/E, 3.8% free-cash-flow yield (stated; no share price stated)
calls.thesis: HOLD — actively bullish and invested (8th-largest position, down ~45% in the drawdown), holding his full position into Tuesday's earnings with cautious optimism; the engagement-problem narrative is a filter that misreads everything (the Warner Bros Discovery bid, watch-time reporting, 6% / ~1,000-job layoffs), and the layoff memo reaffirmed the full-year forecast 6 days before earnings. He believes Netflix is a 25x P/E stock, not 19x.
calls.base_case: Over time Netflix proves profitable, secure, high-margin and reliable enough to rerate to a mid-20s P/E; some uncertainty is fairly priced in, but not the current narrative discount (2022 trough was ~17x).
calls.bull_case: Earnings land in line with the reaffirmed guidance and the engagement story breaks, starting the rerating from 19x towards 25x.
calls.bear_case: Near-term earnings reaction is a coin flip — a 4–7% drop is normal territory for Netflix; engagement grew only ~2% on 200B hours and he concedes the concerns are not completely invalid.

calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 2026-10-12; no flip) — 'well worth holding through the capex cycle'; monetisation power, not pricing power: ad prices +12% YoY while impressions rose +14% and ad revenue +27%, because advertisers bid more for better-converting, more targeted ads across a still-growing daily-active base in every region. Expects a super-strong quarter on Wednesday.
calls.base_case: The business prints a very strong quarter and he holds through the spending cycle.
calls.bull_case: Monetisation keeps compounding — more ads, higher prices per ad, better returns for advertisers — funded by the core apps, including the Muse push.
calls.bear_case: Management likely raises capex guidance again, which could spook investors even on a strong print; the quarter's debate will be Zuckerberg's spending, not the results.

calls.thesis: AVOID — first tracked Joseph TSLA call, no prior stance, no flip: 'not interested in the company' and the Roadster demo 'doesn't convince me to buy the stock' — he cannot buy stocks just because they are cool when the future is already priced in; prefers SpaceX as the more unique, defensible, less competitive Musk investment.
calls.base_case: More of the same: a heavily narrative-driven quarter with little focus on fundamentals.
calls.bear_case: 154x forward P/E on revenue flat for ~2 years, deliveries down, net income down sharply and free cash flow flat; robotaxi rollout is slower, more methodical and more red-tape-bound than promised, against Waymo (~500k rides/week), Uber's multi-brand network and strong Chinese AV rivals.

calls.thesis: BUY — first tracked Joseph MCO call, no flip: Moody's 'still remains one of the best companies in the market' and 'right now it's a particularly strong investment' — the undervalued stock of the title; proprietary, trusted data being integrated across enormous numbers of APIs and businesses, and far more predictable than Netflix, Meta or Tesla reporting the same week (Wednesday, before the open). No position or purchase stated — the call is his stated investment view.
calls.base_case: A predictable compounder: looking out 10 years the company is still in a great position and should deliver very attractive returns.
calls.bull_case: Its unique, trusted data becomes paramount as businesses integrate it via APIs, entrenching the franchise.
calls.bear_case: He 'just doesn't see the weaknesses the market is concerned about' — i.e. the market is pricing concerns he does not share; no specific bear case given.
